extracted.intended_audience: third party conformity assessment bodies; stakeholders submitting comments on CPSC information collection (manufacturers, labs, public interest commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and information-collection requirements for third party conformity assessment bodies seeking CPSC acceptance/continuing accreditation and instructions for submitting public comments on the Paperwork Reduction Act renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials required for CPSC acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for CPSC acceptance of accreditation must be completed by submitting a Consumer Product Conformity Assessment Body Registration Form (CPSC Form 223); an accreditation certificate for ISO/IEC 17025 (General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories); and a statement of scope that clearly identifies each CPSC rule and/or test method for which CPSC acceptance is sought (16 CFR 1112.13(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite 16 CFR 1112.13(a). Independent third party conformity assessment bodies typically submit these documents when applying for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of scope content
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of scope must clearly identify each CPSC rule and/or test method for which CPSC acceptance is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope should explicitly list the CPSC rules/test methods to avoid ambiguity in acceptance. This is a required part of the application package (see 16 CFR 1112.13(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time estimates for initial application by body type
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time to complete initial application materials varies by type of conformity assessment body: 75 minutes for independent third party bodies; longer for governmental and firewalled bodies—8.4 hours for firewalled bodies and 3 hours for governmental bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates are based on historical application data (FY2020–FY2024) and reflect additional requirements for governmental/firewalled entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating existing registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party conformity assessment bodies can update their existing CPSC Form 223 via the CPSC application program rather than submitting a new form; additions to scope are estimated to take 30 minutes each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency observed a large increase in additions to scope (e.g., toys, furniture, batteries, durable nursery products). Estimated annual update workload: 134 additions to scope (20% of ~670 bodies) → ~67 hours annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting identification and subcontract test recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: When a test conducted for purposes of section 14 of the CPSA is subcontracted, the prime contractor's report must clearly identify which tests were performed by a CPSC-accepted third party conformity assessment body acting as a subcontractor, and the subcontractor's test must be appended to the prime contractor's report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal testing records are maintained in the ordinary course of business and not counted as PRA burden; however, CPSC estimates PRA burden for subcontracting-related recordkeeping: assume 5% of bodies subcontract 25% of tests, at ~7 minutes per subcontracted test. Example estimate: 100,500 subcontract tests × 7 minutes = 11,725 hours annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary discontinuation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party conformity assessment body wishing to voluntarily discontinue participation with the CPSC must create and submit required documentation (see 16 CFR 1112.29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated time to complete discontinuation documentation is 30 minutes per body. Historical withdrawals: 106 labs FY2020–FY2024; agency estimates 20 withdrawals per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit frequency and audit submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPSC portion of an audit is required no less than once every two years (16 CFR 1112.35(b)). Labs audited must resubmit updated materials including CPSC Form 223, accredited scope listing, and accreditation certificate. Firewalled and governmental labs must also submit an updated attestation and an employee undue influence memorandum; firewalled labs also must provide a revised risk assessment of impartiality and undue influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on current numbers, CPSC expects ~50% of accepted bodies to be audited each year. Agency estimated time to resubmit updated materials per audited body is ~15 minutes; total audit burden estimated at ~87.5 hours annually (350 bodies × 15 min). Audit burden varies by body type and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory basis and scope of CPSC requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CPSC's rule Pertaining to Third Party Conformity Assessment Bodies (published March 12, 2013) established general requirements and procedures for CPSC acceptance of accreditation, prescribed adverse actions that might be imposed against accepted bodies, amended audit requirements, and amended the CPSC's regulation for inspections; these requirements appear at 16 CFR part 1112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and accepted bodies should consult 16 CFR part 1112 for the full set of obligations, possible adverse actions, audit/inspection rules, and program details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiated requirements by body type (independent, firewalled, governmental)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent, firewalled, and governmental third party conformity assessment bodies have differing procedural requirements and estimated burdens (e.g., initial application time, additional documents, attestations, and risk assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firewalled bodies have additional requirements (e.g., risk assessment of impartiality, undue influence memorandum) and higher estimated preparation/upload times; governmental bodies have other additional requirements and different time estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping baseline vs PRA-countable burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Records maintained in the normal course of business are not considered PRA burden, but certain recordkeeping specifically required by CPSC (e.g., subcontracting identification and appended subcontractor reports) are counted toward PRA burden estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency example: average body maintains records for ~12,000 tests annually; only specific additional recordkeeping activities tied to the information collection are counted in burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated total annual PRA burden and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: CPSC's estimated total annual burden for this collection is approximately 11,977 hours, and at $47.20 per hour (BLS total compensation), the total estimated annual cost is about $565,314.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the agency's current estimate used to support the PRA submission to OMB; commenters may provide data to support revisions to these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions and restrictions for submitting comments (including confidential business information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments identified by Docket No. CPSC-2012-0026 within 60 days via Regulations.gov (https://www.regulations.gov). Do not submit confidential business information (CBI), trade secrets, or other sensitive/protected information through Regulations.gov if you do not want it publicly available. For CBI/trade secrets, submit by mail, hand delivery, courier, or email to cpsc-os@cpsc.gov. All submissions must include the agency name and docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPSC may post all comments without change, including personal identifiers, so use the alternative submission methods for sensitive materials. Docket access: go to Regulations.gov, insert docket number CPSC-2012-0026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested topics for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission specifically solicits comments on: (1) whether the collection is necessary for the proper performance of the Commission's functions, including practical utility; (2) whether the estimated burden is accurate; (3) whether the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected could be enhanced; and (4) whether the burden could be minimized by automated, electronic, or other technological collection techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments addressing these four topics will inform the agency's request for extension of the information collection to OMB; provide data or examples where possible to support assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments on the collection of information by August 11, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received after this date may not be considered in the agency's PRA submission to OMB.
